name: John Dashwood's Urgent Ride
description: John Dashwood rides swiftly on horseback, his face tense and eyes focused ahead. The landscape blurs as he gallops along dirt paths, the rhythm of hoofbeats underscoring the urgency of his journey. Traveling shots follow his progress, capturing the motion and intensity of his passage through the countryside.
related_events: John Dashwood rides horseback in urgent journey

name: Betsy Dyes the Muslin Frock Black
description: Betsy, her eyes red, took the beautiful muslin frock and plunged it into the vat of black dye. The fabric darkened as it soaked, its original appearance fading completely.
related_events: Maid Betsy dyes a muslin frock black

name: Edward Ferrars Arrives at the Estate
description: Edward Ferrars rides up the gravel driveway on horseback, the hooves crunching against the stone. He slows as he approaches the main house, lifting his gaze to the elegant façade.
related_events: Edward Ferrars arrives at the estate on horseback

name: Betsy Hangs Laundry on the Clothesline
description: Betsy steps outside with a basket of laundry and begins hanging clothes on the clothesline. She secures each item with a pin, moving steadily from one piece to the next until the line is filled.
related_events: Betsy pins out laundry

name: Sir John Worries Over Brandon's Delay
description: Sir John stands near his country house, gazing out over the grounds. He speaks aloud, wondering where Brandon could be and expressing fear that the man may have lamed his horse on the journey.
related_events: Sir John expresses concern about Brandon's whereabouts

name: John and Fanny Arrive at Norland
description: John and Fanny's carriage approaches Norland. Fanny speaks, suggesting that they will be in a better position to offer something to those waiting for them.
related_events: Carriage approaches Norland

name: John and Fanny Finalize Their Agreement Before Parting
description: John and Fanny stand ready to leave. John confirms their understanding: no money will change hands, but he welcomes the occasional gift of game and fish when in season. Fanny responds by saying John's father would be proud of him. They exchange no further words before going their separate ways.
related_events: John and Fanny agree on financial arrangement and exchange parting words

name: Servants Load Carriages as Fanny Asks to Help
description: Outside the house, a well-to-do carriage stands parked. Behind it, servants move back and forth, loading trunks and boxes onto an open carriage. Fanny's voice is heard off-screen, asking, 'Help them?'
related_events: Servants prepare carriages for departure

name: Margaret Asks If They Have Arrived
description: Inside the moving carriage, Margaret speaks up and asks if they have reached their destination. The carriage continues rolling forward, the journey still underway.
related_events: Margaret asks if destination is reached
Carriage continues journey

name: Mrs Dashwood Finds Sir John's Letter
description: Mrs Dashwood, breathing heavily, rummages through her wardrobe as gowns are flung aside. She pulls out a particular dress, reaches into its pocket, and withdraws a letter. Holding it in her hand, her expression changes from fury to quiet concern.
related_events: Mrs Dashwood searches wardrobe for gown containing Sir John's letter
Mrs Dashwood retrieves letter from gown pocket

name: Marianne and Elinor Go to Bed in the Cold
description: Marianne and Elinor began undressing for bed, leaving their underclothing on against the cold. They moved quickly, their breath visible in the dim light. As they slipped between the sheets, they both shivered at the touch of the cold linen, their bodies stiffening as they settled into the bed, side by side.
related_events: Marianne and Elinor prepare for bed in cold conditions

name: Margaret Tries to Climb the Impossible Tree
description: Margaret began to climb a tree that was nearly impossible to scale. As she reached up and pulled herself higher, her petticoats caught on a jagged branch. She struggled briefly, then the fabric tore with a sharp rip. She paused, one hand on a branch, skirts now frayed and hanging loose, but did not immediately come down.
related_events: Margaret attempts to climb an impossible tree
Margaret's petticoats snag and tear during the climb

name: Mrs Dashwood Watches Her Daughters Mend
description: Mrs Dashwood stands at the window, gazing out quietly. Mrs Jennings’s words echo in her mind: 'Not a beau for miles.' She turns from the window and looks across the room at her daughters. Elinor and Marianne sit together, carefully mending Margaret’s petticoat. The quiet rhythm of their work fills the space. Mrs Dashwood’s face grows tense, her eyes lingering on them.
related_events: Mrs Dashwood recalls Mrs Jennings's comment about lack of suitors
Mrs Dashwood observes her daughters mending Margaret's petticoat
Mrs Dashwood expresses anxiety about her daughters' futures

name: Fanny and Edward Discuss the Children's Behavior on a Walk
description: Fanny walks with Edward, looking at pictures and expressing her displeasure with the children. She says Miss Margaret is always in trees or under furniture and that Marianne has barely spoken to her civilly. Edward replies that the children have recently lost their father and that their lives will never be the same. Fanny insists that is no excuse.
related_events: Fanny walks with Edward while discussing the children's behavior
Edward reminds Fanny of the children's recent loss

name: John and Fanny Discuss Financial Support Before Leaving London
description: As John and Fanny prepare to leave London, John suggests fifteen hundred as a sum for Fanny's support. Fanny responds by remarking that no brother could do more for his full sisters, let alone a half-sister. John replies that they can hardly expect more. Fanny then shifts the focus to what John can afford, leaving the matter unresolved.
related_events: John proposes fifteen hundred as a sum for Fanny
Fanny reflects on familial duty and financial expectations

name: Elinor Announces Staff Reductions at Norland Park
description: The servants of Norland Park gather in silence in the house's main hall. Elinor stands before them, her voice steady but somber. She informs them that the family is leaving and must downsize their household. Only Thomas and Betsy will be taken to the new home. She looks around at the assembled staff, many of whom have served for years, and says she is deeply sorry to part with them. She assures them that the new Mrs. Dashwood will treat them fairly and with kindness. Thomas and Betsy exchange quiet glances, holding themselves still amidst the heavy silence.
related_events: Elinor announces staff reductions to servants at Norland Park
Elinor expresses regret over dismissing servants

name: Marianne watches the countryside and mimics piano playing
description: Marianne stands by the window, looking out at the wild countryside. Her hand moves slowly up and down along the windowsill, fingers pressing and lifting as if playing a piano, while her gaze remains fixed on the landscape outside.
related_events: Marianne gazes at the wild countryside from the window
Marianne's hand moves rhythmically on the windowsill like playing a keyboard

name: Colonel Brandon Hears Marianne Sing
description: Colonel Brandon dismounts from his horse. From inside the building, Marianne's song begins to rise. He lifts his head sharply toward the windows. A look of pained surprise crosses his face.
related_events: Colonel Brandon dismounts from his horse
Marianne begins singing from within the building
Colonel Brandon reacts to Marianne's song with pained surprise

name: The Dashwoods Await Edward's Promise
description: The Dashwoods are on their way, the mood sombre. Margaret reminds Elinor that Edward promised to bring the atlas to Barton. Marianne looks at Elinor with pleasure and says he will surely arrive within a fortnight. Mrs. Dashwood looks at Elinor with satisfaction.
related_events: Margaret reminds Elinor of Edward's promise to bring the atlas
Marianne expresses confidence in Edward's timely arrival
Mrs. Dashwood looks at Elinor with satisfaction

name: The Dashwoods Arrive as a Boisterous Party Approaches
description: The Dashwoods' carriage draws up at the gate of Barton Cottage, a low and dreary dwelling set in the grey, lonely countryside. At the same time, from the opposite direction, a much grander vehicle approaches, its arrival marked by loud whooping and a lively commotion.
related_events: Dashwoods' carriage arrives at Barton Cottage gate
Grand vehicle approaches with loud whooping

name: Marianne Plays a Sorrowful Tune Despite Elinor's Request
description: Marianne Dashwood sits at the piano, playing a sad piece. Elinor enters the room and asks her to play something less mournful, saying their mother has been weeping since breakfast. Marianne stops playing, turns the pages of her music book, and begins another piece just as sorrowful as the first.
related_events: Marianne Dashwood plays a sad piece on the piano
Elinor enters the room and requests a less mournful song
Marianne turns the page and begins another mournful piece

name: Elinor and Marianne Remove Margaret's Toys
description: Elinor and Marianne began clearing away Margaret's toys. As they worked, Marianne muttered, "Intolerable woman!" Elinor replied, "There is but one consolation—if Edward is anything like Fanny, we shall be only too happy to leave."
related_events: Elinor and Marianne remove Margaret's toys
Marianne expresses disdain toward Fanny
Elinor comments on potential relief from leaving Edward and Fanny

name: Elinor and Betsy Discuss Sugar Prices Amid Budgeting
description: Elinor sits at a small desk, counting coins and making notes. Betsy enters the room to clean out the fireplace. She sees the money on the desk and remarks that sugar costs five shillings a pound in the area. Elinor responds lightly, saying there will be no more sugar then.
related_events: Elinor counts money and makes notes at her desk
Betsy enters the room to clean out the fire
Betsy notices the money on the desk
Betsy comments on the price of sugar in the area
Elinor decides to forgo purchasing sugar

name: Elinor Calls Margaret from the Tree
description: Elinor approaches a large tree and calls out to Margaret, who is hidden in the branches. She tells her to come down because John and Fanny will be arriving at Norland soon. Margaret’s voice comes from above, asking why they are coming to live there when they already have a house in London. Elinor replies that the house passes to John because it is the law—property goes from father to son, not daughter. There is a pause. Elinor then suggests that if Margaret comes inside, they could play with her atlas. Margaret answers that it is no longer her atlas, but theirs. Elinor stands quietly at the foot of the tree, looking up, her expression still as she absorbs what Margaret has said.
related_events: Elinor calls out to Margaret beneath a tree
Margaret questions why John and Fanny are moving to Norland
Elinor explains inheritance law to Margaret
Elinor attempts to coax Margaret inside with the offer of playing with the atlas
Margaret asserts the atlas now belongs to John and Fanny
Elinor reflects on Margaret's statement about ownership

name: Elinor Watches Margaret and Edward Spar Outside
description: Elinor sits by the window, writing a letter. She looks up as Margaret runs past, waving a stick. Edward follows closely behind and begins teaching her how to sword-fight. They move back and forth, feinting and parrying. Edward is serious, guiding her with care. At one point, he turns, as if sensing Elinor’s gaze. She smiles briefly, then looks away.
related_events: Elinor observes Edward and Margaret's sword-fighting from the window
Margaret runs past the window wielding a stick

name: Edward Teaches Margaret Sword-Fighting
description: Margaret runs past the window waving a stick. Edward follows her and takes up a stick as well, showing her how to feint and parry. They move back and forth in earnest play, both focused on the lesson. As they continue, Edward suddenly stops, turning as if aware of someone watching. He looks toward the window where Elinor sits. She smiles briefly but quickly looks away.
related_events: Edward teaches Margaret basic sword-fighting techniques
Edward senses Elinor's gaze and pauses the lesson

name: John and Fanny Decide on Mother's Allowance
description: John and Fanny stand waiting as the ostlers make final adjustments to their carriage. The landlord lingers nearby. John holds out some coins, wondering aloud if giving their mother a hundred pounds a year while she lives would be better than giving her fifteen hundred pounds at once. Fanny takes one of the coins from his hand, nods, and says that if their mother lives more than fifteen years, they would lose out. She adds that people always seem to live forever when there is an annuity to be paid. John then gives the coins to the landlord.
related_events: John considers financial arrangement for their mother
Fanny expresses concern about annuity duration

name: John and Fanny Prepare to Depart and Tip the Landlord
description: John and Fanny stood by as the ostlers made the final adjustments to their carriage. While waiting, John opened his hand to show a few coins. He spoke of leaving a hundred pounds a year to their mother for as long as she lived, wondering if that would be wiser than giving fifteen hundred all at once. Fanny took one of the coins from his palm and nodded in agreement, though she remarked that if their mother lived more than fifteen years, they would be at a loss, as people tend to live a long time when an annuity is at stake. John then handed the coins to the landlord, who had been lingering nearby.
related_events: John and Fanny wait for carriage preparations to finish
John gives coins to the landlord

name: Edward Listens Outside the Door
description: Edward stands outside a half-open door, listening as Elinor speaks inside, trying to persuade Margaret to come out. He hears her pleading, but there is no response. As Fanny approaches with a butler, Edward turns his attention to the wall, pretending to study the mouldings. Fanny passes by without noticing him, continuing down the hall while giving instructions to the servant.
related_events: Edward keeps a discreet lookout outside the door
Elinor attempts to coax Margaret out from hiding
Fanny walks by giving instructions to a butler
Edward pretends to examine the mouldings to avoid suspicion

name: Edward Decides to Intervene
description: Edward stands outside, listening as Elinor speaks through the half-open door, urging Margaret to come out. Her voice is gentle but met with silence. Fanny passes by with a butler, giving instructions, unaware of Edward’s presence. He pretends to examine the mouldings until they move on. After a moment of stillness, Edward straightens, his expression resolving, and takes a step toward the door.
related_events: Edward makes a decision after hearing Elinor's plea

name: Edward and Elinor Ride and Reflect on Their Futures
description: Edward and Elinor ride together on horseback, speaking openly about their lack of purpose and the frustration of having no control over their livelihoods. Elinor remarks that her situation is worse, as she has no prospect of inheritance and no means to earn a living. Edward acknowledges the similarity in their circumstances, then smiles at the irony when she points out that he will inherit his fortune. He is briefly taken aback, but amused by her candor. Elinor adds that neither of them can earn their way forward. Edward muses that perhaps Margaret was right. When Elinor asks what she could possibly be right about, he suggests, half-seriously, that piracy might be their only option. They continue riding in silence for a time. After a pause, Edward asks, 'What is swabbing exactly?'
related_events: Edward and Elinor discuss their lack of occupation and financial dependence
Elinor challenges Edward with ironic remarks about inheritance and gender constraints

name: Edward and Elinor Consider Piracy
description: Edward, smiling, suggests piracy as a solution to their lack of prospects, echoing Margaret’s earlier idea. Elinor responds with quiet amusement, and the two ride on in silence, the notion lingering in the air between them. After a pause, Edward asks what swabbing actually means, his tone curious but light, as if testing the role of a pirate in jest.
related_events: Edward suggests piracy as a humorous solution to financial helplessness
Edward and Elinor ride in silence after discussing bold alternatives to societal norms
Edward inquires about the meaning of swabbing in the context of piracy

name: Elinor and Marianne Review Housing Letters
description: Elinor, Marianne, and Mrs. Dashwood sit around a table with a pile of letters. Elinor hands one letter back to her mother, saying it is too expensive and that they do not need four bedrooms since they can share. Marianne picks up another letter and suggests it as an option. Elinor reads it quickly and responds that they have only five hundred pounds a year, then says she will send out more inquiries that day. At that moment, there is a knock on the door. Edward appears hesitantly, apologizing for the intrusion. He says he believes he has found what they are looking for. Marianne and Mrs. Dashwood look puzzled, but Elinor immediately understands, rising from her seat with a smile of relief.
related_events: Elinor rejects a housing option due to high cost
Marianne proposes a different housing option
Elinor plans to send additional housing inquiries

name: Edward's Unexpected Arrival with a Housing Lead
description: Edward knocked on the door and stepped inside, apologizing for the intrusion. He said he believed he had found what the family was looking for. Marianne and Mrs. Dashwood exchanged puzzled glances, uncertain of his meaning, but Elinor immediately set down the letter she was holding, rose from the table, and smiled in quiet relief.
related_events: Edward arrives with a housing lead
Elinor reacts to Edward's news with relieved understanding

name: John and Fanny Discuss Financial Support for the Women
description: John and Fanny continue their journey, talking about John's promise to provide money to four women. John says that giving twenty pounds from time to time will be enough to fulfill his obligation. Fanny replies that she believes John's father never intended for him to give them any money at all. John points out that the women already have five hundred pounds a year to share among them. Fanny adds that the women have a modest household, with no carriage, no horses, few servants, and little company, so they have no need for more money. She insists they will be quite comfortable as they are.
related_events: John acknowledges the adequacy of periodic financial support
Fanny expresses skepticism about John's father's intentions
John states the annual income shared by four women
Fanny questions the need for additional funds given the women's frugal lifestyle

name: John and Fanny Discuss Money During the Journey
description: John and Fanny ride on together, the road unfolding ahead as they talk. John remarks that twenty pounds from time to time will be enough to fulfill his promise. Fanny agrees, though she admits she believes John’s father never intended for him to give the women money. John points out that the four women will already have five hundred pounds a year to share. Fanny adds that such an amount is more than sufficient—without a carriage, horses, or many servants, and with little company to entertain, their expenses will be small. They conclude that the women will be quite comfortable.
related_events: John and Fanny continue their journey while discussing financial matters

name: Edward Shares His Hopes and Family Pressures with Elinor
description: Edward walks arm in arm with Elinor in the late afternoon sun. He tells her that all he has ever wanted is a quiet, private life, but his mother is determined to see him achieve distinction. She has no clear idea what path he should take—any prominent role will do, whether as an orator, politician, or barrister—so long as he drives his own barouche and moves in high society. Edward speaks lightly, but there is bitterness beneath his tone. When Elinor asks what he truly wants, he says he would prefer to take a position in the church, though his mother finds that too plain. She favors the army, but he finds it too demanding. He admits he hates London, with its lack of peace, and that his ideal life would be in the country, serving a small parish, giving short sermons, and keeping chickens.
related_events: Edward reveals his mother's ambitions for his public distinction
Edward expresses his desire for a quiet private life

name: Edward Speaks of His Vocation
description: Edward walks arm in arm with Elinor in the late afternoon sun. He says he has always preferred the church as a vocation, but his mother considers it too plain. She would rather see him in the army, a path he finds unsuitable. He expresses his dislike of London and his wish for a quiet life in the country, tending chickens and delivering short sermons in a small parish.
related_events: Edward communicates his disinterest in the army and ambivalence toward the church

name: Edward Describes His Ideal Country Life
description: Edward walks arm in arm with Elinor in the late afternoon sun. He says he hates London, finding no peace there. He speaks of wanting a small parish in the countryside, where he could live quietly, keep chickens, and give very short sermons. He says this is his ideal life.
related_events: Edward expresses his preference for a quiet country living over London

name: Fanny and Mrs Dashwood Watch the Garden
description: Fanny stands by the window, looking out at Elinor and Edward as they walk together in the garden. Mrs Dashwood enters, pauses, then moves to stand beside her. The two women watch the couple in silence for a moment. Mrs Dashwood speaks, saying how happy they all are that Fanny invited Edward to Norland, adding that he is a dear boy and much beloved by the family.
related_events: Fanny observes Elinor and Edward walking in the garden
Mrs Dashwood joins Fanny at the window
Mrs Dashwood expresses happiness about Edward's invitation to Norland

name: Fanny Warns Mrs Dashwood About Edward's Prospects
description: Fanny stands by the window, watching Elinor and Edward walking in the garden. Mrs Dashwood enters and joins her, smiling as she sees the couple. She remarks how happy they all are that Edward has come to Norland, calling him a dear boy and saying they are very fond of him. Fanny hesitates, then responds that they have great hopes for Edward, especially regarding his profession and marriage. She adds that their mother is determined both Edward and Robert will marry well. Mrs Dashwood says she hopes their mother also wants them to marry for love, calling true affection the most valuable dowry. Fanny replies that love is well enough, but the heart does not always lead in suitable directions. Lowering her voice, she says Edward is kind and compassionate, the sort who could easily be drawn into a commitment with a penniless woman, and once given his word, he would never break it—though such a match would ruin him. She confides that their mother has made it clear she will cut off all financial support if Edward marries beneath his station. Mrs Dashwood stares at her, her expression shifting to shock and anger. Without speaking, she turns and leaves the room abruptly.
related_events: Fanny comments on expectations for Edward's profession and marriage
Fanny expresses concern about Edward's vulnerability to unsuitable marriage
Fanny reveals conditional financial support for Edward
Mrs Dashwood reacts with appalled understanding to Fanny's implication

name: John Proposes a Financial Gift to Fulfill His Father's Wish
description: John stands in mourning clothes and a traveling cape, watching Fanny Dashwood, who is by a mirror. He tells her he intends to give them three thousand pounds. He explains that the interest from the sum will provide a little extra income and says it would be better to do too much than too little on such occasions. He adds that his father did not specify a particular amount. Fanny remains very still upon hearing this, then slowly turns back to the mirror. She responds, affirming that the sum would more than amply fulfill the obligation. John appears nervous as he speaks.
related_events: John announces intention to give three thousand pounds
John becomes nervous after making his announcement
Fanny reacts with stillness to John's announcement
Fanny turns back to the mirror slowly after John's announcement
Fanny responds affirmatively to John's statement about the sum
John expresses preference for generosity on sensitive occasions

name: John States the Father Did Not Specify a Sum
description: John stands in mourning clothes and a traveling cape, watching Fanny Dashwood as she pauses by a mirror. He tells her that while he feels compelled to help his family, his father did not specify a particular amount. Fanny turns slowly back to the mirror, then looks at him again as John adds that one would rather do too much than too little on such occasions.
related_events: John clarifies that no specific sum was stipulated by the father

name: Fanny Turns to John After Pause
description: After a pause in the conversation, Fanny turns her body and looks at John again.
related_events: Fanny turns and looks at John again after his remark

name: Mrs Dashwood's Outburst at the News of Leaving the House
description: Mrs Dashwood rushes about the room, mourning ribbons flapping, as she packs her knick-knacks into a small valise. She declares it unbearable to be reduced to the status of a visitor in her own home. She speaks of John and Fanny arriving from London at any moment, followed by a flood of relatives who will push them out room by room. Calling the incoming family vultures, she suddenly collapses into a chair and bursts into tears. Elinor watches helplessly, then says she will begin looking for a new house at once, though they have nowhere to go yet.
related_events: Mrs Dashwood expresses outrage at becoming a visitor in her home
Mrs Dashwood anticipates arrival of John and Fanny with extended relatives
Mrs Dashwood denounces incoming relatives as vultures
Mrs Dashwood collapses into a chair and bursts into tears

name: Elinor Decides to Find a New House
description: Mrs. Dashwood rushes about the room, flustered and distressed, stuffing her belongings into a small valise while mourning ribbons flutter behind her. She laments being forced out of her own home, declaring it unbearable to remain and face the arrival of John and Fanny. Overwhelmed, she collapses into a chair and bursts into tears. Elinor stands nearby, watching quietly. She tells her mother they have nowhere to go, then announces she will begin making inquiries for a new house at once. For now, she says, they must endure the others' coming.
related_events: Elinor Dashwood voices concern about having no alternative residence
Elinor Dashwood resolves to begin searching for a new house

name: Mrs Dashwood Packs Her Belongings in Distress
description: Mrs Dashwood moves quickly around the room, stuffing her personal items into a small valise. Her mourning ribbons flutter with each movement. The room is in disarray as she rushes from one object to the next. Elinor stands nearby, watching silently. Mrs Dashwood pauses suddenly, drops into a chair, and begins to cry.
related_events: Mrs Dashwood packs belongings amid emotional distress

name: Marianne Arrives at Breakfast with Tense Politeness
description: Marianne entered the breakfast room where Fanny, Mrs. Dashwood, Elinor, and John were already seated. Elinor caught Marianne's eye and gave a slight nod toward Fanny. Marianne made a face, then turned to Fanny and said, 'Good morning, Fanny,' with careful politeness. Fanny, visibly surprised, replied, 'Good morning, Marianne.'
related_events: Marianne enters breakfast gathering and exchanges polite greetings with Fanny
Elinor signals Marianne with a subtle head motion
Marianne makes a disapproving facial expression

name: Marianne Questions the Silver at Breakfast
description: Marianne entered the breakfast room and greeted Fanny with forced politeness. After returning the greeting, Fanny appeared taken aback. Marianne then asked her how she had found the silver, and whether it was all genuine. Before Marianne could say more, Elinor quickly spoke up, asking when Edward might be expected. Fanny replied that Edward was due the next day, and added that since he would not be staying long, she wondered if Margaret might give up her room for him, as the view from her windows was particularly fine. Marianne slammed her cup down and shot a furious look at Elinor.
related_events: Marianne inquires about the authenticity of the silver
Elinor intervenes to redirect conversation

name: Fanny Requests Margaret's Room for Edward's Visit
description: At breakfast, Fanny suggested that Margaret give up her room for Edward during his short stay, saying the view from her windows was incomparable and that she would like Edward to see Norland at its best. Marianne abruptly slammed her cup down and shot a furious look at Elinor.
related_events: Fanny requests Margaret to give up her room for Edward
Marianne slams her cup and glares at Elinor in anger

name: John and Fanny Study Estate Plans for a Hermitage
description: After dinner, John and Fanny spread out the plans of the Norland estate on the table. They lean over the图纸, tracing lines and discussing possible locations where a hermitage might be built. Their conversation is quiet and focused, carried on in low voices as they consider the layout of the grounds. Meanwhile, Edward begins to read aloud, his voice filling the room. Elino r sits nearby, embroidering in silence, her eyes occasionally lifting to listen. Mrs. Dashwood and Marianne look on, the latter growing restless. When Edward reads a somber passage, Marianne suddenly rises, moves to his side, and takes the book from his hands. She reads the same lines with intense feeling, then urges him to try again. Edward, looking embarrassed, prepares to read once more, catching a quiet, sympathetic glance from Elino r that steadies him slightly.

related_occasions: Evening Gathering After Dinner At Norland

name: Edward Reads Poetry After Dinner
description: After dinner, Edward reads a somber poem aloud to the family gathered in the sitting room. The verses speak of despair and isolation, and his voice fills the quiet space. Elinor sits nearby, her hands moving steadily as she embroiders, her attention fixed on Edward’s words. The others listen in silence, the mood settling into a reflective stillness.
related_events: Edward reads poetry aloud to the gathering
Elinor embroiders while listening to Edward's reading
related_occasions: Evening Gathering After Dinner At Norland

name: Marianne Takes the Book and Reads with Passion
description: After Edward finishes reading a stanza aloud, Marianne rises suddenly, takes the book from his hands, and reads the same lines with intense emotion. She looks at Edward and urges him to feel the poem’s despair, then reads it again with fervor.
related_events: Marianne takes book from Edward and reads stanza passionately
related_occasions: Evening Gathering After Dinner At Norland

name: Elinor's Glance and Edward's Resumption
description: After Marianne took the book from Edward and read the stanza with great passion, Edward, looking mortified, prepared to begin reading again. Before he did, Elinor gave him a sympathetic look. He then started the passage once more.
related_events: Elinor gives Edward a sympathetic look
Edward restarts reading after being corrected by Marianne
related_occasions: Evening Gathering After Dinner At Norland

name: Mrs Dashwood Announces the Move to Barton Cottage
description: Mrs Dashwood told the family that they would be moving to Barton Cottage, a small house offered by her cousin Sir John Middleton on his estate. Edward appeared deeply affected by the news, his face falling at the announcement. Fanny, in contrast, smiled and remarked that a cottage was always very snug. Mrs Dashwood looked first at Edward, then at Elinor, who remained quiet and composed. When Edward asked if they would be leaving before summer, Mrs Dashwood replied that they could no longer overstay their welcome and must depart soon. Margaret chimed in, inviting Edward to come and stay with them. He said he would like that very much. Fanny reminded them that Edward was expected in town by his mother, but Mrs Dashwood did not respond to her, instead telling Edward to visit them as soon as he could and that he would always be welcome.
related_events: Mrs Dashwood announces relocation to Barton Cottage
Edward Devonshire shows devastation over the announcement
Fanny expresses delight at the idea of a cottage
Mrs Dashwood observes Edward and Elinor's reactions

name: Questions About the Move to Barton Cottage
description: John asks about Sir John Middleton’s status upon hearing of the offer of Barton Cottage. Mrs Dashwood explains that Sir John is a widower living at Barton Park with his mother-in-law, who has offered them the cottage. Fanny remarks that a cottage is charming and snug. Edward, looking distressed, asks if they will not leave before summer. Mrs Dashwood replies that they can no longer rely on her sister-in-law’s hospitality and must leave as soon as possible. Margaret interjects, inviting Edward to visit them. Edward says he would like that very much. Fanny reminds the group that Edward is expected in town by his mother, but Mrs Dashwood ignores her and tells Edward to come as soon as he can, assuring him he will always be welcome.
related_events: John questions Sir John Middleton's social standing
Mrs Dashwood asserts necessity of prompt relocation
Edward Devonshire inquires about departure timing

name: Invitations to Barton Cottage
description: Margaret turned to Edward with enthusiasm and asked him to come and stay with them at Barton Cottage. Edward replied that he would like that very much. Fanny interjected, reminding everyone that Edward was expected in town by his mother. Mrs Dashwood did not respond to Fanny, but instead looked directly at Edward and told him to come as soon as he could, adding that he would always be welcome.

She senses his presence and turns, quickly wiping tears from her eyes. He steps forward, offering a handkerchief with a monogram in the corner—ECF. She takes it with a grateful smile. 'Thank you so much for your help with Margaret, Mr Ferrars. She is a changed girl since your arrival,' she says. 'Not at all. I enjoy her company,' he replies. 'Has she shown you her tree-house?' she asks. 'Not yet. Would you do me the honour, Miss Dashwood? It is very fine out,' he says. 'With pleasure,' she answers. They begin to walk away together. 'Margaret has always wanted to travel,' she says. 'I know. She is heading an expedition to China shortly. I am to go as her servant but only on the understanding that I will be very badly treated,' he replies. 'What will your duties be?' she asks. 'Sword-fighting, administering rum and swabbing,' he says. 'Ah,' she replies. As they exit, Mrs Dashwood stands on the middle landing of the staircase, smiling down at them. name: Mr. Dashwood's Final Words to His Family
description: In the dim light of a candlelit room, Mr. Dashwood lies in bed, his skin pale and his breathing slow. Two doctors move quietly around him, their clothing whispering in the stillness. Mrs. Dashwood sits at his side, holding his hand, her eyes fixed on his face. Mr. Dashwood asks urgently if his son John has arrived. She assures him that John is expected at any moment. He speaks of his daughters, saying he has left them little. He hopes Elinor will find a good husband, though he laments the lack of suitable men nearby. He jokes that Marianne will find her romantic hero, and that Margaret will run off to sea and become a pirate. Mrs. Dashwood tries to laugh but nearly chokes on a sob. Thomas, the manservant, enters and announces that John has arrived from London. Mr. Dashwood asks to speak with John alone. Mrs. Dashwood rises, presses John’s hand as she passes, and leaves with Thomas. John takes his place by the bed. Mr. Dashwood tells him that the estate of Norland passes to him by law, and he expresses happiness for John and Fanny. He explains that his wife and daughters will have only five hundred pounds a year, with nothing set aside for the girls’ dowries. He urges John to help them. John, visibly conflicted, promises he will. Mr. Dashwood appears relieved. His breathing changes suddenly. John stands, alarmed, and calls for the doctor. As John rushes to summon help, Mr. Dashwood whispers his final word: 'Help them.'

Margaret then emerges, disheveled and eleven years old, pulling the atlas from under the table and placing it in front of Edward. She announces that the source of the Nile is in Abyssinia. name: Elinor Says Goodbye to Her Horse
description: Elinor strokes her horse’s soft face, her movements slow and tender. She stands quietly with the animal, her expression filled with sadness. The moment passes in stillness, broken only by the horse’s gentle breath.

name: Edward Speaks to Elinor by the Horse
description: Edward approaches Elinor as she stands near her horse, stroking its face. He calls her by her Christian name, 'Elinor,' in a soft and tender tone, causing her to pause. He moves closer and says he must speak with her about something of great importance, his manner earnest and hesitant. The horse breathes between them as he begins to speak of his education, leaving Elinor visibly confused.

name: Edward's Unfinished Confession
description: Elinor says goodbye to her horse, stroking his face as Edward approaches. He asks if she can take the horse with her, then suggests the animal might be useful in the kitchen, though the remark brings only a faint smile. Edward steps closer and addresses her as 'Elinor,' speaking in a tender tone that halts her breath. He says he must tell her something of great importance, drawing nearer as the horse breathes between them. Elinor waits, tense with expectation, but Edward instead begins to speak about his education. He says it was less successful than it might have been, conducted in Plymouth at a school run by a Mr. Pratt. Elinor responds with brief, puzzled replies, repeating his words as he stumbles through the explanation. Before he can continue, Fanny appears, calling Edward's name and waving a letter. She insists he come to London immediately, saying family affairs demand his presence and that his mother is insistent. Edward glances at Elinor with clear frustration, his jaw tight, then excuses himself. Fanny leads him away, leaving Elinor watching them depart.

name: Fanny Interrupts and Takes Edward Away

She tells him he is needed in London immediately, saying family affairs are in chaos and his mother insists on his presence. Edward protests that he is leaving that afternoon, but Fanny dismisses this, insisting it will not do. She remains firm and pulls Edward away. Edward glances back at Elinor with a tense expression before following Fanny, who keeps hold of him as they walk off together.

name: The Dashwoods Arrive at Barton Cottage
description: The Dashwood family steps out of their carriage as Sir John Middleton, a ruddy-complexioned man in a redingote, and Mrs Jennings, a plump, rosy-faced woman, rush forward to greet them. Sir John takes Mrs Dashwood’s hands, ushering her up the path with exclamations of delight. Mrs Jennings asks if the journey was bearable, while Sir John wonders why they didn’t stop first at the Park. They speak over each other, both eager to offer help and hospitality. Mrs Jennings explains she insisted on coming to meet them because they receive so little company. Betsy greets them at the door as Thomas carries in the lighter luggage. Amid the bustle, Marianne slips inside unnoticed. She walks through the parlour, where a feeble fire smokes in the grate, then climbs the stairs and enters a small, bare bedroom. She sits on the bed, rises, opens the window, listens to the voices outside, then closes it and moves to another room, equally plain. With a sigh, she returns downstairs. The others are in the parlour as Mrs Jennings spots her and exclaims over her beauty, declaring her the loveliest girl she has ever seen and urging Mrs Dashwood to find her a husband. Sir John laments there are no suitable young men nearby. Mrs Dashwood begins to look weary under the weight of constant cheer and insistence. Sir John finally suggests they leave the family to settle in.
related_events: DASHWOOD family arrives at destination and is greeted by SIR JOHN MIDDLETON and MRS JENNINGS

name: Marianne Explores the House Alone

She walks into the parlour, where a feeble fire smolders, then climbs the stairs in silence. She enters a small bedroom, sits on the bed, and opens the window. After a moment, she crosses the hall to another bedroom, equally plain, and sighs before turning back down the stairs to rejoin the others in the parlour.

Voices rise from outside—Sir John insisting they must dine at Barton Park every day, Elinor politely suggesting they settle in first. Marianne closes the window, leaves the room, and crosses the corridor to another bedroom, equally plain. She sighs and turns back toward the stairs. As she rejoins the group in the parlour, Mrs Jennings exclaims over her beauty and suggests she be married off quickly, while Sir John laments the lack of young men in the area.

name: Sir John and Mrs Jennings Welcome the Dashwoods with Eager Hospitality
description: As the Dashwoods arrive at Barton Estate, Sir John Middleton and Mrs Jennings rush to greet them with great enthusiasm. Sir John clasps Mrs Dashwood’s hands and ushers the family up the path, insisting they dine at Barton Park every day. Mrs Jennings interrupts, declaring the journey must have been exhausting and expressing how little company they usually have. The two talk over each other, offering constant assurances of help and hospitality. Sir John promises game and fruit will be sent regularly, and the carriage is always available. Mrs Jennings admires Marianne, calling her the loveliest girl she has ever seen, and urges Mrs Dashwood to secure a husband for her quickly. Sir John laments there are no smart young men nearby to court the girls. The remarks hang in the air as Mrs Dashwood, visibly weary, tries to respond with gratitude. Eventually, Sir John suggests they leave the family to settle in.

name: Margaret Watches the Carriage Depart
description: After Sir John and Mrs Jennings climb into their carriage and drive away, Margaret walks down the path, watching until it disappears down the lane. She turns and hurries back to the house, where her mother, Elinor, and Marianne are standing in the parlour. 'They seem very kind,' Margaret says. Mrs Dashwood nods. 'Their generosity is beyond anything I expected.' Elinor, folding her gloves, says, 'Indeed, if they continue at this rate, we may soon be overwhelmed by their kindness.'
